summary: This RFC updates the registry of authentication method results in Authentication-Results header fields, fixing a mismatch between the original registry and the SPF specification. It was replaced by RFC 7001.

plainLanguage.summary: A small fix to a list of result words in email headers, so the words match what the SPF rules say. RFC 7001 later replaced it.

subtitle: Correct SPF result words in email authentication headers

tldr.problem: The email Authentication-Results header registry listed "hardfail" as the result when Sender Policy Framework (SPF) validation failed, but the SPF specification itself used the word "fail".
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6577 marks "hardfail" as deprecated and clarifies that the correct result word is "fail" for SPF failures, aligning the registry with the SPF standard.
tldr.outcome: Replaced by RFC 7001, this fix ensures email implementations use consistent terminology for SPF validation results.

today: RFC 6577 was replaced by RFC 7001. It remains a Proposed Standard and Best Current Practice for email authentication result registries.

sections.title: The Mismatch
sections.content: RFC 5451 created a registry of email authentication method results for Authentication-Results header fields. It listed "hardfail" as the term for SPF validation failures. However, RFC 4408 (Sender Policy Framework) defined the term for explicit failure as "fail", not "hardfail". This inconsistency caused confusion and incompatibility between implementations following one standard or the other.
sections.plainLanguage: One standard said to use "hardfail" but another standard said to use "fail" for the same thing. This document picks the right one.

sections.title: Registry Correction
sections.content: RFC 6577 updates the Email Authentication Result Names registry. It marks "hardfail" as deprecated and updates the "fail" entry to apply to both SPF and Sender-ID methods. A new "Status" column is added to the registry to track which entries are active and which are deprecated. Existing entries are marked as active unless specified otherwise.
sections.plainLanguage: The list of approved words now says "fail" is the right word and "hardfail" is no longer used. Both SPF and Sender-ID should use "fail".

sections.title: Implementation Notes
sections.content: Older implementations may not recognize the corrected term or may still use the deprecated "hardfail". Implementers are advised to support both terms for a transition period. However, some implementations already follow the SPF standard and use "fail", so the fix aligns with existing practice in the field.
sections.plainLanguage: Some old email servers might still use the wrong word, so new servers should accept both for now. But many already use the right one.
